not_eligible_because: simulator-derived: no second independent implementation (dual-extractor rule unmet)
the first-bag metric is bounded by CATALOGUE COVERAGE, not by the matcher: a null means "not these catalogued pages", never "not this opener"
the slot-geometry match is a SHAPE test, not an opener test: 92.5% of Triples match the wiki window against 12.3% of Doubles, over 898 verified T-spins
the ordering metric is scored on 90 of 144 rounds — those holding both a T-spin Double and a T-spin Triple; rounds with only one of the two cannot show an order

the ordering metric names a CLASS, not an opener: harddrop files 38 openers under "Triple Double openers" — C-Spin, Honey Cup, Stray Cannon and Mountainous Stacking among them — and every one of them opens Triple-before-Double

the named-opener match is bounded by how each opener is DRAWN: 299 of 783 catalogue pages are free of a full row and so could ever equal a no-clear opening board; TKI-3 has 12 catalogue pages and none of them qualify, which is why harddrop's own diagrams are carried alongside

the donation metric is bounded by the oracle's GARBAGE HOLE COLUMNS: 23 of 23 donations here sit on a garbage-derived well, and the oracle keeps the engine's own seeded-RNG hole columns, which disagree with the ige-recorded ones 97 of 103 times (oracle-source.ts) — so the shape is counted, but which column any one donation used is not established

wiki_cspin.why: the C-Spin section quotes harddrop in prose; a wiki sentence with no committed copy is a figure whose only home is prose, and nothing re-derives it.
wiki_cspin.provenance_standard: Both revisions carry MediaWiki's OWN rev_sha1 AND a sha1 recomputed here from action=raw. Two independent authorities that agree — the cvc5 standard, not z3's trust-on-first-use. Reproduce: sha1 of the action=raw body, CRLF->LF, trailing newline stripped.
wiki_cspin.the_count_trap: `replaces_the_double` is set by READING each continuation, never by counting headings. Counting them gave 'six non-Double continuations', which is false and shipped to seven reports before this file was written: LST Stacking and T-Spin Triple Tower both describe what happens AFTER a T-Spin Double, and Trinity / STSD branches on whether the TSD was already done, so all three still produce the Double the ordering metric counts. Of the 7 continuations, exactly 1 replaces it.

pages.lead: The C-Spin (TKI積み) is a kind of Triple Double Attack. It is invented by TKI. This name is given because of the "C" shape that is formed by the J and L. As the name suggests, it results in a T-Spin Triple which is usually followed by a T-Spin Double within three bags. As an opener, it is most often built with an ZST core whereas L and J are used to build the overhang.

continuations.heading: T-Spin Triple and Imperial Cross
continuations.first_sentence: No matter how wide the gap between the overhang and the stack on the right is, you can replace the T-Spin Double with a T-Spin Triple or Imperial Cross after the T-Spin Triple from any C-Spin setup.

continuations.heading: STMB Cave
continuations.first_sentence: The STMB Cave continuation will only work if the following cells in diagram 1 (marked with X's) are free.

continuations.heading: Trinity / STSD
continuations.first_sentence: If you used a J piece as the overhang and there is an S piece or nothing on the overhang, you can make a Trinity (if the TSD is not done beforehand) or STSD (if the TSD is done beforehand) by placing an S piece on the overhang.

continuations.heading: Fractal
continuations.first_sentence: If you have a 4-columns wide gap, you can place the third bag's Z and S pieces as the base, if the second Z piece was placed on the overhang.

continuations.heading: LST Stacking
continuations.first_sentence: Generally, if you have a 2-columns wide gap, you can follow with LST Stacking by placing an L piece on the overhang.

continuations.heading: T-Spin Triple Tower
continuations.first_sentence: If there is a Z piece on a J piece overhang, regardless if that Z piece is from the second or third bag, you can stack a T-Spin Triple Tower after a T-Spin Double.

pages.lead: The Triple Double attack, also known as Triple-Double, C-Spin, or abbreviated as TD, is a combo T-Spin setup that consists of a T-Spin Triple followed by a T-Spin Double.
pages.empty_field: Empty field Triple Double setups are also known as C-Spins.

wiki_cspin.the_tension: the two pages do not agree. Triple_Double_Attack_Setups equates an empty-field Triple Double with a C-Spin outright, which would make the ordering metric the wiki's own definition; C-Spin attributes the name to the C shape formed by J and L, says the Double is 'usually' the follow-up, and gives one continuation that replaces it. So Triple-then-Double OVER-counts and UNDER-counts. Recorded, not resolved: a wiki contradicting itself is not a licence to adopt the reading that flatters the metric.

cell_legend.0: the window was verified to its end and the order did not happen
cell_legend.1: a T-spin Triple then a T-spin Double, both inside the opener window, both observed
cell_legend.null: the verified prefix ended before the window did and nothing was seen — UNKNOWN, not zero. A 1 needs no such caveat: an observed order cannot be undone by an unobserved remainder, so truncation loses C-Spins and never invents one

column_legend.cspin_order: the Triple-then-Double order. 0/1 on a per_round row (a round either showed it or did not); on a per_match row, how many of that match's SCORED rounds did
column_legend.tspin_doubles_window: T-spin Doubles at lock <= window_pieces — the population the order above is decided on, and NOT the round's T-spin count
column_legend.tspin_doubles: T-spin Doubles over the WHOLE round, from the replay's own results.stats.clears.tspindoubles — the twice-extracted field facts.json carries, which tspinCounterCheck proves this simulator reproduces on every round. null is UNKNOWN (the round carried no counter), never zero

ordering.denominators: THE TWO SIDES OF A ROW ARE NOT THE SAME ROUNDS, and dividing one into the other is the mistake this note exists to stop. cspin_order sums over SCORED rounds only — a round whose opener window the verified prefix never reached is in rounds_unscored and contributes nothing — while the T-spin counters come from the replay and cover every round of the match. cspin_order <= min(tspin_doubles, tspin_triples) therefore still holds, because the C-Spin side can only lose rounds; "this share of those spins were C-Spins" does not follow and must not be printed. The bound is asserted at build time

session_perfect_clears.source: report/facts.json (clears.allclear, read independently by extract.py and extract2.ts)
session_perfect_clears.means: an upper bound on completed Perfect Clear Openers: a session cannot hold more completed PCOs than it holds perfect clears, whatever the opening fields looked like — and a session with none cannot hold one at all. Which of them arrived early enough to BE a PCO is `perfect_clear_timing`, and that answer comes from the simulator

perfect_clear_timing.source: the oracle board source (runCaseOracle), checked per round against the replay's own results.stats.clears.allclear — the field extract.py and extract2.ts read into facts.json

donation.definition: plugging the well with a piece so a T-spin can clear the rows across it, the clear then re-opening the well surface-to-floor — the plug is a loan, not a wall

counter_anchor.source: the replay's own per-kind T-spin counters (results.stats.clears.tspindoubles and its seven siblings) — the fields extract.py and extract2.ts read into facts.json as tspin_doubles etc., so they are twice-extracted and inside the trust chain
counter_anchor.covers: the DENOMINATOR only. The tables' numerators — which of those clears was a donation or a cave — come from this simulator alone and stay quarantined

dual_engine.covers: a CHECK on the verdicts, not a re-scoping of the tables — they still score the oracle's verified prefix. Read `agreement_on_positives`, never `agreement_overall`: both verdicts are rare, so the overall rate is negatives agreeing with negatives

donation.means: how many verified T-spin clears were fired across a plugged well that the clear then re-opened — every filled cell of that column lay inside the cleared rows, with at least 4 empty cells walled beneath it. The naive reading of the technique ("the well was filled through the cleared rows") is FORCED BY ARITHMETIC — a full row requires every column filled — and so fires on 100% of all T-spin clears, which is proved rather than measured (NaiveClauseForced, spec/DonationCave.dfy); the same predicate at these thresholds without the re-opening clause fires on 31.96% of this session's 898. The discriminating clause is the re-opening, and that is what is counted here. That figure is THIS SESSION's and no other: the corpus band belongs to whatever can see every session, which this file cannot
donation.caveat: every donation in this corpus sits on a GARBAGE-derived well, and the oracle board source keeps the engine's own seeded-RNG hole columns, which disagree with the ige-recorded columns 97 of 103 times (see oracle-source.ts). So the count says the board offered this shape that often; it does not establish WHICH column any one donation used, and it may never be read as "this player donated into that well"

stmb_cave.definition: a floating T-spin Double placed over a cave at least three columns wide — the cave is OFFSET from the T, sharing two of its three columns, so the test is overlap with the T's span and never containment

counter_anchor.source: the replay's own per-kind T-spin counters (results.stats.clears.tspindoubles and its seven siblings) — the fields extract.py and extract2.ts read into facts.json as tspin_doubles etc., so they are twice-extracted and inside the trust chain
counter_anchor.covers: the DENOMINATOR only. The tables' numerators — which of those clears was a donation or a cave — come from this simulator alone and stay quarantined

dual_engine.covers: a CHECK on the verdicts, not a re-scoping of the tables — they still score the oracle's verified prefix. Read `agreement_on_positives`, never `agreement_overall`: both verdicts are rare, so the overall rate is negatives agreeing with negatives

stmb_cave.means: how many verified T-spin Doubles landed over a >= 3-wide gap overlapping the T's columns. Read it against BOTH controls beside it and never on its own: `min_depth_histogram` says how deep those gaps were, and a one-row-deep 3-wide gap is a dimple rather than a cave; `triple_control` counts the same shape under T-spin Triples, where it is ordinary TST residue
